title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page and Customer Comms Templates
author: Ava Chen
summary: Company-wide on-call and incident response playbook covering incident lifecycle, role definitions, runbook templates, postmortem process, rotation policy, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates.
body:
Overview:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard incident process. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, product owners, support, and any teams that own production services. Use this document as the canonical source for incident lifecycle, runbook structure, escalation rules, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation guidance, and standardized communication templates for customers and the status page.

Primary goals:
- Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR).
- Ensure consistent, timely customer communications.
- Capture actionable postmortems and drive remediation.
- Maintain healthy, predictable on-call rotations and capacity.

1) Incident severity definitions (severity and impact buckets):
1. Sev0 / SEV-0 (Critical): Production-wide outage or system impairment that affects all customers or causes data loss; immediate pager pages. Target MTTR: < 30 minutes for detection and initial mitigation.
2. Sev1 / SEV-1 (High): Major degradation for a large subset of customers or a critical feature is unavailable.
3. Sev2 / SEV-2 (Medium): Localized degradation or minor loss of functionality for a subset of users; no immediate pager for secondary unless escalated.
4. Sev3 / SEV-3 (Low): Informational or minor issues with low user impact; handled during business hours.

SLO & alert thresholds (examples):
- API 95th percentile latency: target < 250ms; alert: p95 > 500ms for 10m.
- Request error rate: target < 0.5%; alert: 5xx rate > 1% for 5m.
- Queue backlog: target < 1000 items; alert: queue depth > 5000 for 5m.

2) Roles & responsibilities:
- Primary on-call (Pager): First responder, runs initial triage and executes runbook steps. Responsible for timely escalation.
- Secondary on-call (Backup): Supports primary; takes over if primary needs relief or issue escalates.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team activity for Sev0/Sev1. Manages timeline, decisions, and resource allocation.
- Communications Lead (Comms): Prepares status updates for the internal channel and status page; coordinates customer-facing messages with Support/CS.
- Service Owner / SME: Technical owner of the impacted service; provides deep-dive guidance and approves mitigations.
- Postmortem Author / Owner: Writes the postmortem within the SLA window and tracks action items until closure.

3) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step):
1. Detection & Triage (0-15 minutes):
   - Pager fires or a customer report is received. Primary acknowledges within 5 minutes.
   - Runbook: confirm scope and severity, check dashboards, error rates, recent deploys, and related alerts.
   - If initial triage indicates Sev1/Sev0, escalate to Secondary and declare IC.
2. Mobilize (15-30 minutes):
   - IC assigned (rotate if necessary). Open a dedicated incident Slack channel and create an incident incident doc (link template below).
   - Communications Lead posts an initial internal summary and prepares a public status page message if customer-visible.
3. Mitigate (ongoing):
   - Follow service-specific runbook steps (see Runbook Templates). Execute safe mitigations first (rollback, traffic diversion, instance restart).
   - Use canary/feature flags where applicable to reduce blast radius.
   - Track actions in the incident doc, with timestamps and owners for each action.
4. Communicate (30m+):
   - Post cadence: initial internal update at 30 minutes, public status update at 60 minutes if customer impact confirmed, then every 60 minutes or on major milestones.
   - Use the status page templates below; coordinate with CS to surface high-touch customer notifications.
5. Recover & Confirm (when mitigated):
   - Ensure system health has returned to SLOs for a sustained period (30 minutes default).
   - Confirm with monitoring and SMEs; collect logs and artifacts for postmortem.
6. Post-incident actions (within SLA):
   - IC closes the incident once resolved and confirms condition with primary metrics.
   - Postmortem must be created within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev0 and assigned to an owner.
   - Action items are tracked and must include owner, due date, and verification steps.

4) Runbook template (service-specific runbook example):
- Title: <service-name> runbook
- Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: <service-owner>
- Pager channel: #pager-<service>
- Symptoms: list of observable signals (e.g., >5xx rate, queue depth)
- Quick checks (ordered):
  1) Check grafana dashboard: dashboards/production/<service> - key panels: api-error-rate, latency, CPU, GPU utilization
  2) Check recent deploys: git commit history and deployment window (last 30 mins)
  3) Check logs: prod-logs cluster / service logs: e.g., kubectl logs -n prod -l app=<service> --tail=200
- Mitigation steps (ordered from least to most disruptive):
  1) Restart worker process: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<service>-worker -n prod
  2) Scale up replicas: kubectl scale deploy/<service> --replicas=<n>
  3) Route traffic to previous stable cluster: runbook script: /ops/runbooks/switch-traffic.sh <cluster-id>
  4) Rollback last deploy: ./deploy rollback --service <service> --to <sha>
- Escalation path: primary -> secondary (10m) -> on-call manager (20m) -> ENG leadership (40m)
- Post-incident: collect heapdumps, pprof profiles, and attach to incident doc.

Runbook quick actions (CLI snippets):
- Check pod errors: kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=<service> --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- Tail logs: kubectl logs -f -n prod $(kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=<service> -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
- Recreate problematic node: gcloud compute instances delete <node-id> --zone=<zone> (on private infra coordinate with infra team)

5) Escalation and paging policy:
- Primary must acknowledge within 5 minutes. If no acknowledgement, Pager escalates to Secondary after 5 minutes, then to On-call manager after additional 15 minutes.
- For Sev0, automated escalation to ENG leadership occurs after 30 minutes if unresolved.

6) On-call rotations and schedule guidance:
- Rotation model: weekly rotation for primary on-call (Mon 08:00 UTC -> next Mon 08:00 UTC). Secondary rotates on the same cadence but offset by one week where feasible.
- Shift length: 1 week primary, on-call handoff in the rotation playbook.
- Handoffs: each on-call must publish a short handoff note that includes ongoing incidents, scheduled maintenance, and known trouble areas.
- Time off and holiday coverage: request shift swaps in the oncall calendar and confirm 72 hours before your shift. If no swap available, engage manager to arrange coverage.
- Burnout policy: after 6 on-call weeks in 3 months, team members should be offered one week of on-call-free time or an additional secondary coverage allocation.

7) Game days (runbook validation exercises):
- Frequency: At least quarterly per critical service.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, measure MTTR, exercise cross-team communication, and test status page workflows.
- Typical scenarios: API unavailability due to DB failover, model server GPU OOM, control plane auth outage, regional network partition.
- Structure: planning (owner/roles, objectives), dry-run (walkthrough), live exercise (simulate alerts), postmortem & metrics review.

8) Postmortem process & template (requirements):
- Timeline: Postmortem must be drafted within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev0 and published within 7 days. For Sev2/Sev3, publish within 14 days based on impact.
- Must include:
  - Title (concise), severity, incident timestamp range, impacted services and customers, total duration, and authors.
  - Executive summary (1-2 sentences).
  - Timeline (annotated, minute-grained where possible).
  - Root cause analysis (RCAs) with evidence; include contributing factors.
  - Mitigations applied during incident.
  - Long-term fixes and action items (owner, due date, verification criteria).
  - Follow-up tasks: monitoring, test coverage, runbook updates, runbook game day assignment.
  - Severity review: was severity assigned correctly? If not, explain.

Postmortem template (markdown-ready):
- Title:
- Severity:
- Incident start / end:
- Summary:
- Impact:
- Timeline:
- Root cause:
- Mitigations during incident:
- Long-term fixes / action items (owner / due date):
- Lessons learned:
- Links: incident doc, runbook, dashboards, logs

9) Status page and customer communications templates
- Status page principles: be factual, transparent, and timely. Avoid speculation and internal jargon. Give clear guidance for customers (workarounds, ETA if known).

Initial public status update (template):
- Title: [Major Outage] <service-name> experiencing elevated error rates
- Impact: Users may see increased errors and elevated latency when calling <endpoint>.
- Time detected: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Current status: Investigating
- Root cause: (TBD)
- Mitigation steps under way: traffic reroute, rolling restart of workers, increased capacity
- Next update: in 60 minutes or when status changes

Follow-up update (template):
- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Summary: Progress update — mitigation in progress, error rate reduced from X% to Y%
- Next steps: continue monitoring, execute rollback if required
- Next update: in 60 minutes

Resolution update (template):
- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Summary: Service returned to normal; monitoring shows metrics at/under SLOs
- Root cause: brief statement of root cause and contributing factors
- Mitigation and long-term fixes: short list and link to postmortem
- Customer guidance: any customer-facing cleanup steps if required

High-touch customer email template (for major incidents):
- Subject: Redwood Inference service incident update — <service-name> (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Body: Dear <Customer>,
We experienced an incident affecting <service-name> between <start> and <end>. During the incident you may have observed <impact>. Our team mitigated the issue by <short mitigations>. We are conducting a full postmortem and will share findings and fixes within 7 days. We apologize for the disruption. If you need immediate assistance, please reach out to <support-contact> or your account team.
Best,
Redwood Inference Support

10) Incident documentation artifacts (must be attached to incident record):
- Incident doc (chronological log), runbook references used, dashboard screenshots, alert graphs, relevant logs, deploy SHAs, and postmortem link.

11) Metrics and reporting:
- Weekly on-call metrics: number of pages, average acknowledgement time, average resolution time, top alerting services.
- Quarterly reliability review: trends in MTTR/MTTA, action item completion rate, postmortem backlog.

12) Security and compliance notes:
- If incident involves customer data exposure or access control failure, notify Security and Legal immediately and mark incident confidentiality as "restricted". Follow the security incident response playbook and preserve evidence.

13) Templates and links:
- Incident doc template: /confluence/templates/incident-doc-template
- Postmortem template: (see above) and /confluence/templates/postmortem-template
- Runbook checklist: /confluence/eng-sre/runbook-checklist
- On-call calendar & rotations: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rotations-schedule

14) Ownership and maintenance:
- Document owner: eng-sre team (oncall-process-maintainers@redwood.example)
- Review cadence: annual review or after any Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- How to propose changes: edit the doc and add reviewers; major changes require approval from SRE manager and at least one service owner.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline snippet (format):
- 2026-02-15 09:12 UTC: Pager fired — elevated 5xxs for inference-api
- 09:14 UTC: Primary acknowledged
- 09:18 UTC: IC declared and incident channel created (#inc-inference-2026-02-15)
- 09:30 UTC: Traffic diverted to canary cluster
- 09:52 UTC: Error rate fell below threshold; monitoring confirmed stability at 10:30 UTC
- 10:05 UTC: Incident resolved; postmortem assigned to @m.singh

Appendix B — Quick escalation contact list (internal):
- On-call manager: oncall-manager@redwood.example
- SRE lead: sre-lead@redwood.example
- Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.example
- Customer success escalation: cs-escalation@redwood.example

Contact and feedback:
If you have suggestions or find inaccuracies in this playbook, please propose edits or email oncall-process-maintainers@redwood.example.

End of document."
